newsitem.title: USA: Argosy sees more competitive pressures.
newsitem.headline: Argosy sees more competitive pressures.

text.p: Argosy Gaming Co said it expects competitive pressures on its revenues and profit margins to intensify in months ahead.
"To counter these competitive pressures, the company will now focus on additional cost reductions and expense controls which have been recently identified," Argosy said.
The riverboat casino operator Friday reported a net loss for the third quarter on lower revenues compared to last year.
"Argosy has experienced increased competitive pressures which have impacted revenues and margins at all of its operating properties," the company said.

The company showed a third-quarter loss of $0.32 per share after charges, versus a year-ago profit of $0.07 per share. Revenues on the quarter were $60 million, down from $66.6 million in the year-ago period.

"This decrease is primarily due to the decrease in casino revenues and the elimination of admission charges February 1996 due to competitive pressures at the Argosy Casino in Riverside, Mo.," the company said.
Casino revenue fell "due to the new, expanded and enhanced competition in the Iowa, Kansas City and St. Louis markets over the past nine months," Argosy said.

Argosy added, "The company also anticipates additional new casinos to begin operations in the St. Louis and Kansas City marketplaces over the next several months, which will continue to put pressure on its revenues and margins in these highly competitive markets."
